title: Unsafe hostels ignore HYDRAA's 3-month move-out warning

slides.head: Unsafe hostels ignore HYDRAA's 3-month move-out warning
What happened
slides.body: Several hostel managements in Hyderabad and Cyberabad have not vacated unsafe premises or added safety measures despite HYDRAA's warning.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: HYDRAA Commissioner AV Ranganath gave the warning after the August collapse at Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli.

slides.head: HYDRAA hostel inspections begin
slides.body: Operators say they signed 1-3 year leases worth lakhs and complying could shut hostels across the city.

slides.head: Dig deeper
slides.body: Operators say they hold leases of 1-3 years paid in lakhs, so they won't move.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: HYDRAA's inspections from January 1 and whether any hostels are sealed or demolished. Ask: Where would residents go if many hostels shut at once?

slides.body: Hyderabad news in 30 seconds, with the numbers and the questions. Follow for tomorrow's drop: spillthetea.news

captions.instagram:
Unsafe hostels ignore HYDRAA's 3-month move-out warning

After a seven-storey illegal hostel building collapsed at Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli in August killing two workers, HYDRAA told operators to shift to safe buildings within three months. Many have not, Telangana Today reports; inspections start January 1.

Why it matters: HYDRAA Commissioner AV Ranganath gave the warning after the August collapse at Anjaiah Nagar, Gachibowli.

Source: Telangana Today. Image: Telangana Today
